items.title: Green exceptional intersection families
items.statement: Fix a finite group G, a p-subgroup P and N_G(P)<=H<=G. Write ^gQ=gQg^{-1}. Put X={P intersect ^gP:g outside H}, Y={H intersect ^gP:g outside H}, and Z={Q<=P: no G-conjugate of Q lies in a member of X}. Relative family-projectivity means every nonzero indecomposable summand is relatively projective for a member of that family; the zero module qualifies, including for the empty family. The classes in the correspondence consist of modules having a vertex in Z.
items.strategy: Define X,Y as actual finite families, not as sets of all smaller subgroups. Interpret conjugate containment existentially. For family-projectivity use every indecomposable direct summand so the definition does not presuppose a selected decomposition. Never call all members of Y proper subgroups of P. The formula makes sense for P=1 and H=G; the latter gives empty X,Y and every Q<=P in Z. This is a definition only; later lemmas prove independence and decomposition claims.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Complete finite-family definition with left conjugation, existential conjugate containment, all-summands family predicate, zero/empty and P=1/H=G boundaries. Read both exact supplier definitions and Saunders pp36-37 family interface; no arbitrary-dimensional projectivity/AC clause is consumed. Explicit-path rendering passes; definition has proof not applicable.

items.title: Green exceptional family containment and fusion
items.statement: For Q<=P, containment in a G-conjugate of X, an H-conjugate of X, and an H-conjugate of Y are equivalent. Every X-member is proper in P; P belongs to Z. G-conjugacy between two Z-members is realized in H. No Y-member contains an H-conjugate of a Z-member.
items.strategy: If ^gQ<=P intersect ^sP with s outside H and g in H, H-containment is immediate. If g is outside H, Q<=P intersect ^(g^{-1})P already. H-X containment implies H-Y containment. If ^hQ<=H intersect ^sP, h in H and s outside H, then Q<=P intersect ^(h^{-1}s)P. This proves all equivalences. Equality P=^sP would put s in N_G(P)<=H, so X-members have smaller order than P. If ^gQ=R with Q,R in Z and g outside H, then R<=P intersect ^gP, contradiction. These are finite subgroup arguments and require no AC. Do not infer that Y-members have smaller order.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Authored all three containment implications with explicit conjugators, proper X intersections, P admissibility and full H fusion; Q=1/P=1/H=G computed explicitly without AC. Read Saunders Lemma4.35 and current local definition. Explicit-path precheck/render and strict proof contract pass after canonical phase adoption.

items.title: Green vertex retention and inducing lift
items.statement: Finite G, field k of characteristic p>0, finite-dimensional left modules, and nonzero indecomposables. Assume AC when invoking the inherited Krull–Schmidt/finite-length prerequisite chain; its use is the DC-dependent chain-condition converse, not finite coset representatives. If M has vertex Q and Q<=L<=G, (a) Res_L M has an indecomposable summand with Q as a vertex, and (b) there is an indecomposable L-module U with vertex Q and M dividing Ind_L^G U. These are separately chosen witnesses; do not claim they coincide yet.
items.strategy: For (b), choose source S at Q, decompose Ind_Q^L S and extract U whose induction contains M. A vertex T of U may be conjugated in L into Q. Induction transitivity makes M relatively T-projective; vertex containment gives |Q|<=|T|<=|Q|, hence T=Q. For (a), S has full vertex Q since a proper relative inducing subgroup would induce M from that subgroup. Extract U from Res_L M with S dividing Res_Q U. Mackey applied to M dividing Ind_Q^G S gives a vertex T of U with |T|<=|Q|. Mackey on S dividing Res_Q Ind_T^L Res_T U forces Q<=^lT for some l in L. Orders give equality, so Q is a vertex of U. Apply the explicit tensor/function equivalence in the examined inherited Mackey argument; all splittings and decompositions are finite. AC is retained for the inherited finite-length argument.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Complete separate inducing and restriction witnesses: source has full Q vertex; induction extraction gives T<=Q and equal orders; two restriction Mackey decompositions force Q to be a conjugate of the restriction vertex. All named interfaces read in full, finite-dimensional hypotheses checked, inherited DC/AC stated. Precheck, rendering and strict contracts pass; outside-run draft Mackey publication remains serial-owner work, not a missing mathematical argument.

items.title: Green mackey intersections force proper vertices
items.statement: Finite G, field k of characteristic p>0, finite-dimensional left modules, and nonzero indecomposables. Assume AC when invoking the inherited Krull–Schmidt/finite-length prerequisite chain; its use is the DC-dependent chain-condition converse, not finite coset representatives. For relatively P-projective H-module U, Res_H Ind_H^G U is U direct sum E with E relatively Y-projective. Restriction takes relatively X-projective G-modules to relatively Y-projective H-modules. Induction takes H-modules which are both relatively P-projective and relatively Y-projective to relatively X-projective G-modules. Only X forces proper-subgroup vertices; Y excludes vertices in Z.
items.strategy: Choose finite W with Ind_P^H W=U direct sum Uprime, using Higman. Mackey for Res_H Ind_P^G W gives Ind_P^H W direct sum E0; off-H terms are induced from H intersect ^gP. Mackey for H back to H gives Res Ind U=U direct sum E and Res Ind Uprime=Uprime direct sum Eprime. Krull–Schmidt cancellation implies E direct sum Eprime is isomorphic to E0, so E is Y-projective; membership alone would not give this cancellation. For restriction of X-projectives, Mackey subgroups lie in H intersect ^tP intersect ^(ts)P with s outside H. At least one of t,ts is outside H, so these lie in a Y-member. For the converse decompose U; each vertex can be chosen Q<=P and is H-contained in Y. The preceding family lemma makes Q G-contained in X, so transitivity of induction gives X-projectivity. All error families are summand-closed by Krull–Schmidt. AC use is inherited finite-length decomposition only.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Actual proof supplies finite Higman witness, cancellation of U plus Uprime in two Mackey expansions, outside-H t/ts restriction transport, and vertex-containment induction transport. Empty families and zero inputs computed. All dependency arguments examined; strict contracts, explicit precheck and rendering pass. Inherited AC stated.

items.title: Green restriction has one distinguished summand
items.statement: Finite G, field k of characteristic p>0, finite-dimensional left modules, and nonzero indecomposables. Assume AC when invoking the inherited Krull–Schmidt/finite-length prerequisite chain; its use is the DC-dependent chain-condition converse, not finite coset representatives. For a G-module M with vertex Q in Z, Res_H M=U direct sum E, where U is indecomposable with vertex Q, occurs once, E is relatively Y-projective, and M divides Ind_H^G U. In particular this applies to Q=P; no other summand has a vertex in Z.
items.strategy: Use inducing lift to choose U with vertex Q and M dividing Ind U. U is relatively P-projective, so Res Ind U=U direct sum E0 with E0 Y-projective. Krull–Schmidt puts Res M inside this decomposition. Independently vertex retention supplies a summand W of Res M with vertex Q. The family lemma excludes W from E0, so W is the single copy U. Cancellation then gives Res M=U direct sum E with E dividing E0. Any further Z-vertex would be Y-projective, contradicting the family lemma. This proves the inverse-direction summand witness M dividing Ind U as part of the construction, rather than invoking the later inverse theorem. AC only through the stated inherited decomposition chain.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Written noncircular restriction proof: separate inducing and restriction witnesses, Y exclusion, finite multiset comparison giving exactly one U and summand-closed errors. Registered explicit transitivity/splitting supplier. All seven interfaces examined; explicit precheck/render and strict contracts pass; AC and identity boundaries stated.

items.title: Green induction has one distinguished summand
items.statement: Finite G, field k of characteristic p>0, finite-dimensional left modules, and nonzero indecomposables. Assume AC when invoking the inherited Krull–Schmidt/finite-length prerequisite chain; its use is the DC-dependent chain-condition converse, not finite coset representatives. For an H-module U with vertex Q in Z, Ind_H^G U=M direct sum E, with M indecomposable of vertex Q occurring once, E relatively X-projective, and U dividing Res_H M. There is exactly one summand with a vertex in Z.
items.strategy: Res Ind U=U direct sum Yerror, where U is not Y-projective. Decompose Ind U into indecomposables and assign its unique copy of U on restriction to one summand M. Every summand has a vertex T that can be chosen inside Q, by transitivity and vertex containment. For every other summand W, Res W is Y-projective; retention supplies a restriction summand of vertex T. Thus T is H-contained in Y and the family lemma makes T G-contained in X; W is X-projective. M cannot be X-projective because restriction of such a module is Y-projective. Its chosen T<=Q<=P therefore lies in Z. Apply the preceding restriction lemma to M: its unique non-Y summand has the same vertex T and must be U. Hence T is H-conjugate to Q, so Q is itself a G-vertex of M. This also proves uniqueness and multiplicity one without the typographical x/z confusion in Saunders 4.38. AC as in the preceding lemmas.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Full induction proof assigns unique U on restriction, forces all other terms into X using retained vertices, excludes X for the distinguished term, then uses the already authored restriction lemma to identify its vertex with Q. Explicit vertex-conjugacy dependency added. Finite-dimensional/AC/identity boundaries checked; precheck, render and strict contracts pass.

items.title: Green distinguished summands are mutually inverse
items.statement: Finite G, field k of characteristic p>0, finite-dimensional left modules, and nonzero indecomposables. Assume AC when invoking the inherited Krull–Schmidt/finite-length prerequisite chain; its use is the DC-dependent chain-condition converse, not finite coset representatives. The restriction and induction distinguished-summand assignments on the Z-vertex classes satisfy g(f(M)) isomorphic to M and f(g(U)) isomorphic to U, and depend only on isomorphism classes.
items.strategy: The restriction lemma includes M dividing Ind f(M); induction has exactly one non-X indecomposable there, and M is non-X because its vertex is in Z. Thus g(f(M)) isomorphic to M. The induction lemma includes U dividing Res g(U); restriction has exactly one non-Y indecomposable there, and U is non-Y by the family lemma. Thus f(g(U)) isomorphic to U. Functors preserve isomorphisms and Krull–Schmidt fixes multiplicities. Do not compare merely orders of vertices or select canonical vector-space representatives. AC is only inherited decomposition support.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Both inverse identities are proved separately using the actual summand witnesses from the preceding constructions; induced/restricted isomorphisms and unique finite multiplicities give class-level well-definedness. Explicit identity/zero/choice cases and item-specific contracts checked; precheck/render/strict contracts pass.

items.title: Green correspondence with exceptional families
items.statement: Finite G, field k of characteristic p>0, finite-dimensional left modules, and nonzero indecomposables. Assume AC when invoking the inherited Krull–Schmidt/finite-length prerequisite chain; its use is the DC-dependent chain-condition converse, not finite coset representatives. With N_G(P)<=H<=G and X,Y,Z as defined, restriction and induction give inverse bijections between isomorphism classes of indecomposable kG-modules and kH-modules having a vertex in Z. Correspondents have a common vertex Q in Z, Res_H M=f(M) direct sum Yerror and Ind_H^G U=g(U) direct sum Xerror, with the indicated relative family-projectivity. No assertion about a common source is included.
items.strategy: Assemble the two constructions and inverse lemma, including multiplicity-one and error clauses. A vertex is a subgroup up to conjugacy, so use the family fusion lemma through the constructions to reconcile representatives; assignments themselves are on module isomorphism classes. When H=G both error families are empty and errors vanish. If P=1 the normalizer hypothesis forces H=G. Preserve the finite-dimensional and nonzero restrictions and the inherited AC assumption.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Full Z-class Green theorem assembled from completed constructions, with each map landing in the correct domain, both inverse identities, multiplicity one, different X/Y errors, common vertex and identity boundaries. All exact supplier statements/proofs examined; precheck/render/strict contracts pass; AC inherited and no common-source claim.

items.title: Green correspondence for modules of vertex exactly p
items.statement: Finite G, field k of characteristic p>0, finite-dimensional left modules, and nonzero indecomposables. Assume AC when invoking the inherited Krull–Schmidt/finite-length prerequisite chain; its use is the DC-dependent chain-condition converse, not finite coset representatives. In particular the isomorphism classes of indecomposable modules having P as a vertex correspond under N_G(P)<=H<=G. Restriction errors are Y-projective and induction errors X-projective; these need not have identical subgroup families.
items.strategy: Every P intersect ^gP for g outside H has order smaller than P. Hence P is in Z; specialize the theorem to vertex P. Correspondents have the same vertex and the inverse preserves it. No smaller-vertex claim about all restriction errors, no extension to arbitrary H, and no common-source assertion. Inherited AC as above.

title: Vertices Sources and the Green Correspondence — Examples

items.title: Green restriction summand with the same vertex
items.statement: Assume AC for the inherited general Green-correspondence identification. Let k be a field of characteristic 2, G=S_3, P=H={1,(12)}, and M=k with trivial G-action. Then N_G(P)=P, M has vertex P, and Res_H^G(M)=k is its sole indecomposable summand, also with vertex P. Thus the Green correspondent is the one-dimensional trivial kH-module. The explicit trace calculations themselves use no choice.
items.strategy: Use the six permutations of {1,2,3}. Conjugation sends (12) to (g(1) g(2)); normalizing its two-element subgroup forces g to preserve {1,2} and fix 3, hence g is 1 or (12). Every action matrix on M is [1], and one-dimensional nonzero modules are indecomposable. For trivial action, every k-linear endomorphism is scalar lambda, and the relative trace from Q is [G:Q] lambda. The three-coset trace from P of id is 3 id=id in characteristic 2, so Higman gives relative P-projectivity. The trace from 1 of any scalar is 6 lambda=0, so M is not relatively 1-projective. As 1 is the only proper subgroup of P, P is a vertex. Restricting leaves the same one-dimensional trivial module: it is relatively H-projective (index 1), but the trace from 1 is 2 lambda=0, so its vertex is P=H. Dimension one admits no additional nonzero direct summand. The exact-P Green corollary therefore identifies this sole summand as the correspondent. No claimed concrete Farrell example or common-source conclusion is used.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Explicit S3 normalizer, 1x1 action matrices and characteristic-2 relative traces 3=1,6=0,2=0 prove both vertices and the sole restriction summand. Applied exact-P theorem only after all hypotheses verified, with inherited AC. Generated leaf-example provenance retained; precheck/render/strict contracts pass.

items.title: Green correspondence for a trivial intersection subgroup
items.statement: Finite G, field k of characteristic p>0, finite-dimensional left modules, and nonzero indecomposables. Assume AC when invoking the inherited Krull–Schmidt/finite-length prerequisite chain; its use is the DC-dependent chain-condition converse, not finite coset representatives. For a nontrivial TI Sylow p-subgroup P of G and H=N_G(P) properly contained in G, the Green correspondence matches all nonprojective indecomposable G- and H-modules and both errors are projective. Include H=G as the identity case separately.
items.strategy: For g outside H, TI gives P intersect ^gP=1. Since P is normal Sylow in H, any p-subgroup H intersect ^gP is contained in P, so it too is trivial. Thus X=Y={1} and Z consists of nontrivial subgroups of P. Higman trace for Sylow shows every indecomposable has a vertex conjugate into P. Relative 1-projectivity equals projectivity, so vertex 1 is precisely the excluded projective case. Apply the full theorem, not merely its exact-P specialization. For H=G the error families are empty and the correspondence is the identity on all modules; its nonprojective restriction is still an identity. Do not add Saunders’s unproved aside that all projective error summands are isomorphic. AC is explicitly inherited, including the general relative-1/free-summand equivalence.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Computed X=Y={1} from TI and the normal Sylow quotient; scalar relative trace puts every vertex into P, and both vertex-1/projective directions identify the full nonprojective domains. Added explicit vertex-containment supplier; distinguished H=G empty-family case. All seven inputs examined; precheck/render/strict contracts pass; AC propagated.

items.title: Green correspondence identity boundaries
items.statement: Finite G, field k of characteristic p>0, finite-dimensional left modules, and nonzero indecomposables. Assume AC when invoking the inherited Krull–Schmidt/finite-length prerequisite chain; its use is the DC-dependent chain-condition converse, not finite coset representatives. If H=G, restriction and induction are identity functors and the Green assignments on their stated domain are identity maps; X=Y are empty. If P=1, the normalizer hypothesis forces H=G, and the exact-P correspondence is the identity on projective indecomposables.
items.strategy: N_G(1)=G forces H=G. Tensor multiplication G over G and its inverse identify induction with the module itself, while restriction changes no action. A nonzero indecomposable cannot have a nonzero complementary summand in itself; the empty error families also force zero errors. P=1 selects projective indecomposables through relative 1-projectivity. Keep zero outside the indecomposable domain and distinguish all-Z classes for H=G from the exact-P specialization. AC only for inherited prerequisites.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Explicit balanced tensor multiplication and inverse give identity induction; empty families and indecomposability force zero errors. P=1 forces H=G and both relative-1/projective directions identify the fixed-vertex domain. All four interfaces read, inherited AC retained; precheck/render/strict contracts pass.
